extracted.intended_audience: patent holders, potential patent challengers, in-house counsel, and parties considering post-issuance patent review options
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on eligibility, filing prerequisites, and strategic considerations for pursuing or defending a Covered Business Method (CBM) patent review before the PTAB as a post-issuance validity challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered Business Method patent definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A CBM patent is defined as a patent directed to a method or corresponding apparatus for performing data processing or other operations used in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include activities incidental to, or complementary to a financial activity; not strictly limited to products or services of the financial services industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO definition compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To be subject to CBM Review, the patent must meet the definition according to the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is determined against the USPTO's standards; meeting that statutory/regulatory definition is a prerequisite to CBM Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner standing / filing prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: To file a petition for CBM Review, the challenger must show it has been sued or charged with infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM Review is not an open-to-all challenge mechanism; actual litigation or an accusation of infringement directed at the challenger is required to establish standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nexus requirement between infringement and CBM patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The infringement asserted against the challenger must be directed to a covered business method patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must tie the alleged infringement to a patent that satisfies the CBM definition; if the asserted patent is not a CBM, CBM Review is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary institution by the PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM Review is not automatically instituted; institution is a matter of PTAB discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition does not guarantee institution — the PTAB must determine whether to institute review (e.g., reasonable likelihood standards or other institution criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudicative forum and decision-makers
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM Review is adjudicated by a panel of Administrative Patent Law Judges in the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) at the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM Review is intended to be similar to a validity challenge that would ordinarily take place in federal district courts, but is decided by the PTAB rather than a district court judge or jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBM Review as a cost-effectiveness consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM Review can be a more cost-effective option to challenge a patent than federal litigation may provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should weigh CBM Review as a potentially lower-cost alternative to district court litigation for attacking patent validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic defense guidance for patent holders
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent holder faced with a CBM Review petition should consider providing arguments at the outset to avoid institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-drafted, early arguments could convince the PTAB that there is not a reasonable likelihood the challenger will prevail, thereby avoiding institution of CBM Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBM Review as a post-issuance validity challenge option
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM Review provides a means to challenge the validity of an issued patent as part of post-issuance proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM is one post-issuance pathway (alongside IPR, PGR, reexamination, etc.) for addressing patent validity; parties should select the procedure that best fits the patent's subject matter and procedural prerequisites.
